findings.summary: Witness B's claim that she had a clear, unobstructed view of Vehicle A all the way to impact is physically impossible from her marked position on Exhibit 4.
findings.detail: In her deposition, Witness B testified repeatedly that she stood outside in front of the store and had 'a clear view of the car the whole way in' and 'watched it right up until the moment it hit. Nothing was in the way' (Depo Witness B 41:10-41:20, 52:00-52:07, 56:00-56:18). However, when asked to mark her standing position on the overhead intersection diagram (Exhibit 4), she placed red pen mark #2 at [8.5, 0, 9.0] m on the south edge of the bench shelter (Depo Witness B 1:54:24-1:54:50). Witness D testified that this shelter has a roof and a solid sheet-metal back panel (Depo Witness D 09:51-10:29). Both the witness-eye render (wit_witness_B_t9p9.png) and the independent ray-cast check confirm that from [8.5, 0, 9.0] m at eye height 1.57 m (5 ft 6 in), Witness B's sightline to Vehicle A is completely blocked across all 25 sample positions within a 2 m radius—first by the bench shelter's back panel (occ_bench_shelter) and second by the red truck-tractor and semitrailer (veh_truck_tractor / veh_semitrailer) crossing NE 140th Court.

evidence.citation: bench shelter footprint at X=7..10 m, Z=7.5..9 m
sightline wit_witness_B→veh_car_a: blocked by occ_bench_shelter and veh_truck_tractor (25/25 samples blocked within 2 m)

findings.summary: Witness A's account of seeing Vehicle A crest the hill for several seconds before the turning semitrailer blocked his view is physically consistent with the reconstruction.
findings.detail: Witness A (modeled on the real westbound motorist) stated he was driving westbound on US-27A at about 60 mph roughly a quarter mile east of the truck when he saw the dark sedan crest the hill and descend eastbound for 2 to 3 seconds before the turning semitrailer entered the eastbound lanes and blocked his view (witness_A.md p.1; docket_hp_att4_witness_interview.txt p.5-6, p.12; docket_vehicle_dynamics_study.txt p.8 Table 2). The independent sightline check at t=4.0 s confirms an unobstructed line of sight from Witness A's driver eye to Vehicle A (553.6 m, 25/25 samples clear), and the subsequent motion of the 53-ft semitrailer across the eastbound lanes occludes Vehicle A prior to impact at t=10.43 s.

evidence.citation: sightline wit_witness_A→veh_car_a @ t=4.0s: pass (25/25 clear, 553.6 m)

findings.summary: Witness C's account from his stopped pickup in the westbound inside lane west of the crossover is physically consistent with the reconstruction.
findings.detail: Witness C stated he was stopped in the westbound inside lane about 18 m west of the NE 140th Court crossover, watching the tractor-trailer pull slowly out of the turn lane and swing across the eastbound lanes, when he heard the crunch and saw the car emerge from the far side of the trailer (witness_C.md p.1). The overhead render and independent sightline check at t=10.43 s confirm an unobstructed line of sight (35.0 m, 25/25 samples clear) from Witness C's pickup to the semitrailer.

evidence.citation: sightline wit_witness_C→veh_semitrailer @ t=10.43s: pass (25/25 clear, 35.0 m)

findings.summary: Witness D's testimony that she was inside the retail store behind the register and could not see the highway or the collision is physically consistent with the reconstruction.
findings.detail: Witness D testified she was working behind the counter register inside the retail store restocking cigarettes when she heard the loud bang, and that she could not see the highway from the register because of the drink cooler, shelving, and window posters, plus a solid west wall facing NE 140th Court (Depo Witness D 06:39-09:24, 18:02-18:52, 41:26-42:18). The independent ray-cast check from [24.0, 1.6, 15.0] m confirms her sightline to Vehicle A at impact is blocked by bld_retail_store.

evidence.citation: sightline wit_witness_D→veh_car_a @ t=10.43s: blocked by bld_retail_store

findings.summary: Daylight solar geometry, clear dry weather, deactivated vehicle headlights, and absence of sun glare in the renders match the documentary record and NOAA solar calculations.
findings.detail: For May 7, 2016 at 4:36:12.7 p.m. EDT (UTC-04:00) at 29.4106° N, -82.53979° W (docket_har1702.txt p.15, p.32 fn.40; docket_tech_recon_factual.txt p.16), the expected sun position is azimuth 265.0° (W) and elevation 45.1° (shadow bearing 85° E). The world's authored directional light matches this exactly (azimuth 265.0°, elevation 45.1°, 0.0° error), casting eastward shadows in overhead_t9p9.png and chase_veh_car_a_t9p5.png. The sky is clear and the asphalt is dry (docket_har1702.txt p.15; Depo Witness B 23:04-23:47), Vehicle A's headlights are off per ECU data (docket_driver_assistance_factual.txt p.7-8), and no witness or driver has sun glare risk (smallest sun-to-sight-line angle is 45.0° for Witness A and 45.1° for Witness A's pickup travel direction, well above the 30° elevation / 15° cone glare threshold). No real scene footage or scene photographs exist in the case media files (which contain only simulated depositions and schematic Exhibit 4), so lighting was compared against the documentary record and computed solar position only.

evidence.citation: expected sun az 265.0 / el 45.1 vs render az 265.0 / el 45.1; min sun angle 45.0 deg (wit_witness_A); glareRisk false for all witnesses and drivers

critique.summary: The physical reconstruction confirms a direct contradiction in Witness B's testimony: from the exact position she marked on Exhibit 4 ([8.5, 0, 9.0] m, on the south side of the bench shelter), her line of sight to the oncoming eastbound sedan (Vehicle A) is doubly obstructed by the opaque sheet-metal back of the bench shelter and by the turning tractor-semitrailer (Vehicle T) in the seconds before impact. Accounts from Witness A (westbound driver), Witness C (stopped westbound driver), and Witness D (store clerk inside behind the register) are physically consistent with the scene geometry and sightlines. A Round 5 patch is applied to refine four vehicle-kinematics measurements so the car's center starts slightly west of the 345 m hill crest (giving the full 10.4 s mutual sight time), the tractor-semitrailer combination spans the exact 71 ft 7 in (21.82 m) length, impact occurs 45 ft 5 in (13.84 m) aft of the tractor front, and the utility pole strike occurs at 8.4 s post-impact.

findings.detail: For May 7, 2016 at 4:36:12.7 p.m. EDT (UTC-04:00) at 29.4106° N, -82.53979° W (docket_har1702.txt p.15, p.32 fn.40; docket_tech_recon_factual.txt p.16), the expected sun position is azimuth 265.0° (W) and elevation 45.1° (shadow bearing 85° E). The world's authored directional light matches this exactly (azimuth 265.0°, elevation 45.1°, 0.0° error), casting eastward shadows in overhead_t9p9.png and chase_veh_car_a_t9p5.png. The sky is clear and the asphalt is dry (docket_har1702.txt p.15; Depo Witness B 23:04-23:47), Vehicle A's headlights are off per ECU data (docket_driver_assistance_factual.txt p.7-8), and no witness or driver has sun glare risk (smallest sun-to-sight-line angle is 45.0° for Witness A and 45.1° for Witness A's pickup travel direction, well above the 30° elevation / 15° cone glare threshold). No real scene footage or scene photographs exist in the case media files (which contain only simulated depositions and schematic Exhibit 4), so lighting was compared against the documentary record and computed solar position only.
